links.note: Substitutes n = 15 into the degree-1 rule 2n - 1 to get 29. No constant difference is used, so it is evaluating the ax+b form rather than the linear-pattern concept 1372.
Classifies 200 + 50m as a linear polynomial against quadratic, cubic and constant. It is the ax+b definition being applied to a cost rule.
Builds 4x for the perimeter of a square of side x, against x^2, 2x and x+4. The work is assembling the right algebraic expression from a situation.
The common difference of 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 is 2 - the constant difference between consecutive terms, which is this concept's definition.

V(t) = -25t + 500 is water draining at a constant 25 litres a minute, so the coefficient is negative and the quantity falls by a fixed amount per interval. That is linear decay; the zero at t = 20 is when the tank empties.
Checks the evaluation of 9x + 7 at x = 3 as 34. It tests substitution into an expression, not any classification. (Options A and C are both true as printed - see report.)
Names 7x - 4 as a linear polynomial of degree 1 against quadratic, constant and not-a-polynomial. The ax+b definition with a non-zero is what decides it.
4 notebooks at Rs x and 2 pens at Rs 15 assemble to 4x + 30; the distractors mis-assemble the terms. Building the expression correctly is the whole task.
A Rs 50 fixed charge plus Rs 12 a kilometre gives 50 + 12x; every distractor attaches the numbers to the wrong part (50x+12, 62x). Assembling terms and constants correctly is 1368.
4x + 5y + 3 from pens in red and blue boxes plus 3 spare. It has two variables, so it is not a univariate polynomial at all - it is expression-building, 1368.
Fencing needs 2[(x+5) + 3] = 2x + 16, so the expression has to be formed and then simplified. The near-miss 2x+10 comes from dropping the breadth.
A temperature x rising by 8 gives x + 8, against 8x, x-8 and 8-x. Translating the situation into the right expression.
Diagnoses (5x+8) - (2x+3) wrongly given as 3x+11: the constants should go 8 - 3 = 5. The error is in handling the constant terms of an expression.
Recovers the rule linking the two table columns as 3x + 4 - a y = ax + b relationship between two variables, which is what the answer states, rather than just the size of the difference.
Asks what the constant 100 in B(x) = 25x + 100 means: the fixed charge, i.e. the bill at x = 0. Interpreting b as the value where the line starts is this concept.
6x + 5 - (2x - 3) is 4x + 8, so Student B is right; Student A failed to change the sign of the -3. Simplification of terms and constants, not classification.
p(x) = 10x + 30 is given as a linear polynomial and evaluated at x = 5 to give 80. The distractor 50 is the variable part alone, ignoring b.
Refutes the claim that the constant -3 in M(n) = 8n - 3 is the first output: -3 is the value at n = 0, and M(1) = 5. That the constant is the value at zero is exactly the y-intercept concept.

Part (c) turns on 15 being the increase in score PER ITEM in P(x) = 15x + 40 - the coefficient read as a rate of change. That interpretation of a is the slope concept; the constant 40 is secondary here.

Finds and verifies the zero of P(x) = 4x - 20 at x = 5. A degree-1 polynomial with a non-zero has exactly one zero, which is why the item works; the set has no separate zero or x-intercept concept, so 1371 is the home.
Derives the rule P(x) = 3x + 4 from the table and then uses it at x = 0 and x = 10. The deliverable is the y = ax + b relationship between the two variables.
